chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about water that nothing renders impure. He said: “Kurr.” He said: I said: “And what is kurr?” He said: “Three spans by three spans.”

key_terms.الْكُرُّ: kurr, the defined threshold quantity of water in jurisprudential usage
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the substance under discussion in the ruling of ritual purity
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْبَارٍ: three spans, a unit of dimension used to describe the measure
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: anything; any impure matter or contaminant
key_terms.كُرٌّ: the legal measure of a substantial amount of water that resists becoming impure
key_terms.لَا يُنَجِّسُهُ: is not rendered impure; does not become najis through contact

ai.seo_question: What is the quantity of kurr water that is not rendered impure by contact with impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the quantity of water that is not rendered impure by contact with impurity. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام identifies this as kurr water and describes it with a measured dimension, making it foundational in discussions of ritual purity in fiqh.
